newsitem.title: USA: Telecomm Industries, Unitel plan merger.
newsitem.headline: Telecomm Industries, Unitel plan merger.

text.p: Telecomm Industries Corp said Thursday it has signed a letter of intent to acquire by merger Unitel Inc, a computer and telephony systems integrator.
Terms of the proposed transaction were not disclosed.

The merger is subject to the execution of a defintive agreement, completion of due diligence, approval of Telecomm's board after obtaining required consents and other customary terms and conditions, it said.
Telecomm said it anticipates closing the deal in the second quarter of 1997.
Telecomm is Ameritech Corp's largest distributor. Ameritech is a Chicago-based telephone and cable television service provider.

Telecomm said that the merger, when completed, will create one of the largest non-manufacturer communications integrators in North America, with combined revenues of more than $21 million and more than 20 locations in Indiana, Ohio, Kentucky, Michigan, Illinois and Wisconsin.
The client based of the merged entity would include more than 20,000 accounts and locations, it said.
As a combined entity, the two companies have additional relationships with GTE, BellSouth, AT&. LCI Long Distance, Sprint, and other long distance and local exchange carrier relationships, it said.
Under current plans, the seven locations of privately held Unitel's would combine with more than 15 Telecomm sites to form a regional products and services vendor. Unitel is based in Indianapolis.
James Lowery, chairman and chief executive of Telecomm, said the merger is a "natural fit" for the two companies.
Paul Satterthwaite, president of Unitel, said the two companies' expertise in total systems communication integration "will be a tough combination to beat."
